title: A rotational obstruction to prescribed-end Veech realization
verdict: PASS for the attributed prescribed-matrix obstruction to three nonplanar ends.

native.printed: 14 October 2026, no numeric version in PDF

actual.support: Inspected original arithmetic checker and archive scope. Independent reviewer authenticated all 133 distribution entries and 27 pinned original files.

proof: Uniformization of the actual surface gives a nonabelian discrete deck group in PSL(2,R). A normalizing sequence approaching the identity would centralize two noncommuting elements, contradicting the abelian centralizer of every nonidentity element. A finite system of compact local lifts ensures properness descends to quotient automorphisms.

A core joining n≥3 one-ended nonplanar arms is not displaceable: an alternate copy in one arm would leave all n−1 other ends in one complement component, while every complement component is the image of a single-end arm.

The entire preimage D⁻¹(SO(2)) acts holomorphically, including any translations in the kernel, so properness and the core force it to be finite. Its derivative image is all of Γ∩SO(2). Included finite cone points extend holomorphically by removability on the same surface; excluded points are not filled. Complete Poincaré metric of this conformal structure puts no completeness constraint on the given flat metric.
A=(3+4i)/5 preserves the norm. Traces of integer matrix powers obey u_{m+1}=6u_m−25u_{m−1}, and u_m≡1 mod 5 for every m≥1, whereas a positive identity power would have trace 2·5^m.

independent.result: The exact native three-page manuscript proves the prescribed-matrix obstruction it claims. No material mathematical gap or unfulfilled imported hypothesis was found. It is an explicitly credited corollary/application of earlier results, rather than a new general finiteness theorem or a firstness claim.

scope: A counterexample with a specific matrix generator. One or two ends, abstract cyclic groups with another generator, lattice and finite-area questions are outside the claimed theorem. Credits earlier results for the full mechanism. No follow-up cleared the required bar.
